newsitem.title: UK: Tatarstan official says no Eurobond issue in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Tatarstan official says no Eurobond issue in 1997.

text.p: The Republic of Tatarstan does not plan to issue a debut Eurobond until next year, a senior official said on Tuesday.

Marat Mortazine, first deputy minister at the ministry of foreign relations, told a conference in London that Tatarstan would not tap the capital markets until after its main oil company AO Tatneft had done so.
"Tatarstan is absolutely new to the capital markets, and we had a dilemma how to enter them," Mortazine said.
"We decided that oil company Tatneft should enter the Eurobond market first, and only after that, in 1998, we will start with Eurobonds for the Republic of Tatarstan," he said.
Mortazine said Tatneft was already known to investors because it had issued American depositary receipts (ADRs) last year.
Tatarstan is an autonomous Russian republic.
Its president Mintimer Shaimiyev said in May Tatarstan would issue a Eurobond by the end of the year.
Shaimiyev said he expected Tatarstan to receive a credit rating no lower than the ratings on Russia's sovereign Eurobonds.
Russia's sovereign Eurobonds are rated Ba2 by Moody's, BB- by Standard & Poor's and BB+ by IBCA.
In March, Tatarstan's finance ministry said it had recommended Dresdner Kleinwort Benson as underwriter for Tatneft's Eurobond.
